role: calibration only (sibling n = xyz − x − y − z: its failures are prime-value conjunctions)
missing_theorem: PROVED here (identity): (xy − 1)(xz − 1) = x(n + x) + 1, so n is represented iff some x ≥ 2 has x² + nx + 1 = de with d ≡ e ≡ −1 (mod x), d, e ≥ 2x − 1. At x = 2 the class condition is automatic, so n is represented whenever 2n + 5 is composite. All 708 exceptions in (10³, 10⁵] have 2n + 5 prime; 324 also have 3n + 10 prime. The enrichment n ≡ 3 (mod 6) is the mod-3 admissibility of {2n + 5, 3n + 10, …}. The sibling is a tied-divisor lottery with Crocker-like low slices, so Pass 1's Poisson e^{−29} comparison was mis-specified.
barrier: B2 (same tied-divisor shape); low slices are primality events (H-type failures)
next: Close. Lesson: in a sibling where the smallest level's class condition is vacuous, failures are driven by prime values of the low-level integers. ES's level-1 class condition is not vacuous (4p + 1 needs a prime ≡ 3 mod 4).
note: Explains the 'not finite-looking' exception set. It is (★)-like rather than ES-like.
